title: TF Hunt - Office application starts a shell
query: event.code: "1" and process.parent.name: ("WINWORD.EXE" or "EXCEL.EXE" or "OUTLOOK.EXE") and process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "cmd.exe" or "mshta.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "rundll32.exe")

control.query: event.code: "1" and process.parent.name: ("wscript.exe") and process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "cmd.exe" or "mshta.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "rundll32.exe")
control.why: No capture has Office starting a process. The control swaps in the script host from the Empire VBS launcher to prove the fields and value lists match.

title: TF Hunt - Executable content written to Downloads or Temp
query: event.code: "11" and file.path: (*\\Downloads\\* or *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*) and file.extension: ("exe" or "dll" or "js" or "hta" or "lnk")

control.why: Files written to user Temp in the captures are a LSASS dump and PowerShell policy-test scripts, none with these extensions. The control drops the extension clause to prove the path wildcards match.

title: TF Hunt - DNS lookups of a reported domain
note: Template. The validation value is a benign domain present in the captures; it checks the field mapping, not a phishing detection.

title: TF Hunt - OT commands from the phished workstation
TF Hunt - Encoded PowerShell on the host
query: event.code: "1" and host.name: "<host>" and process.name: "powershell.exe" and process.command_line: (*-enc* or *-EncodedCommand* or *FromBase64String*)

title: TF Hunt - Process access to LSASS on the host
TF Hunt - Service or scheduled task created on the host
TF Hunt - OT commands from the infected host
query: source.ip: "<host IP>" and network.protocol: (modbus or s7comm or dnp3)

title: TF Hunt - Failed logons for a wrong password or an unknown user
note: The two 4625 events in mdec_4625_denied_account_restriction have SubStatus 0x0 (account restriction) and are correctly excluded.

title: TF Hunt - Account lockouts
note: No capture contains a lockout (4740); none of the brute-force captures reached a lockout threshold.

title: TF Hunt - Five failures then a success for the same account on one host
query:
sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=10m
  [authentication where event.code == "4625"] with runs=5
  [authentication where event.code == "4624"]

control.query:
sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=10m
  [authentication where event.code == "4625"] with runs=5
control.why: No capture has a successful 4624 after the failures. The control keeps only the five failures to prove the join keys and categories match: both accounts in the local brute force must produce a sequence, and spraying, one failure per account, must not.
